sheets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: high-resolution character turnaround/reference sheet for later 3D modeling, based ONLY on the attached ORIGINAL reference image, not any existing mesh or previous rendered zombie.
Input image 1 is the character identity, proportions, pose, palette and material reference.
Recreate this exact friendly classic normal zombie as polished tactile 3D animated-film/clay CGI: large grey sage-green bald head, softly irregular scalp with fine pores and faint forehead creases, several sparse bent black hairs, unequal large yellowed ivory eyes with very small dark pupils, organically recessed dark olive eye sockets and blended fleshy brows (never goggles or separate black rings), tiny two nostrils and a nearly absent nose, open dark brown mouth with five irregular cream teeth (three upper, two lower). Its anatomical LEFT eye (viewer-right in front view) is larger.
Crucial volumetric requirement: the cranium is a plump, rounded, three-dimensional ovoid, with a substantial rounded occiput extending behind the face; the sagittal front-to-back depth must be comparable to head width. Show a clearly round dome and full rear skull in side/three-quarter views, NOT a thin disc, slab, flattened mask, human skull, or oversized long nose. Keep the original front silhouette and head-to-body proportions, not a new character design.
Outfit: worn brown open jacket with soft notched folded lapels, loose wrinkled bent sleeves and cuffs, aged ivory collared shirt and ragged lower hem, long faded red tie with diagonal off-white stripes, indigo blue worn trousers, broad rounded brown leather shoes. Anatomical RIGHT leg (viewer-left in front view) has the long trouser leg and irregular knee hole exposing green skin. Anatomical LEFT leg (viewer-right in front view) has a jagged short torn trouser leg exposing the green knee and pale shin, with loose blue denim bunched at the ankle. Maintain these anatomical sides in every view, do NOT mirror the damage. Preserve the reference asymmetrically hunched posture, two arms gently reaching forward, relaxed hanging hands with five rounded fingers each, slightly spread feet, slight head tilt. Head largely hides the short neck.
Medium and materials: the same soft cinematic 3D rendering language as the reference: finely mottled matte skin, gently textured worn brown fabric, woven tie, blue denim, softly scuffed leather. Real rounded organic surfaces and cloth thickness. Avoid plastic shine, metallic skin, flat cutout edges, exaggerated zombie gore, harsh contour lines, low-poly faceting.
Backdrop: clean neutral warm light-grey studio background, subtle soft contact shadow, no scenery, house, lawn, walnut, props, extra characters or watermark. Diffuse neutral studio light revealing volume, consistent color and light across all panels. The three panels must depict ONE internally consistent character, with identical anatomy, clothing details and pose rotated in space; not three different designs.
Composition: wide horizontal model sheet with exactly THREE evenly spaced full-body orthographic views, equal scale, full hair and shoes visible, aligned soles and head heights. Left panel FRONT 0 degrees. Middle panel anatomical LEFT SIDE exact 90-degree profile (nose faces screen left), clearly show deep rounded rear cranium and forward-reaching arms in profile. Right panel BACK exact 180 degrees. Camera remains eye-level; only rotate the character. Ample clear space between views. Small unobtrusive clean sans-serif sheet title "A" and panel labels exactly "FRONT", "LEFT SIDE", "BACK". Detailed useful model references, not silhouettes.
